correctness.rationale: The bounded quadratic identity holding on a dense subset extends to all vectors. Real polarization applied to the self-adjoint part of \(D=K-T_FT_G^*\) proves \(D+D^*=0\) and no stronger identity. A fresh symbolic reconstruction checks \(F=(e_1,e_2)\), \(G=((1,-1),(1,1))\), \(K=I\), \(T_FT_G^*=\begin{pmatrix}1&-1\\1&1\end{pmatrix}=I+J\) with \(J^*=-J\ne0\); its quadratic form is \(x^2+y^2\) for every vector, while reconstruction fails. Both displayed sequences are Riesz bases. For any bounded real skew-adjoint \(J\), setting \(g_j=(I-J)e_j\) gives \(T_FT_G^*=I+J\); the estimate \(\|(I-J)x\|^2=\|x\|^2+\|Jx\|^2\) and the same adjoint estimate show bounded invertibility, hence Riesz bases.
correctness.risk: The complex Hilbert branch remains valid by complex polarization; the objection applies specifically to the stated real branch.

final_claim: In the real self-adjoint \(K\) branch of Li--Li Remark 1.2, the diagonal scalar reconstruction condition for Bessel families \(F,G\) is equivalent to \(K=(T_FT_G^*+T_GT_F^*)/2\), not to full \(K=T_FT_G^*\). Every bounded skew-adjoint defect can occur, even with Riesz bases.
